title: Charges API for a payments platform

license.attribution: Written for ReadCode. Not affiliated with any payments company.

questions.text: Walk through what POST /charges does when the request carries an Idempotency-Key header that this account has already used. Cover both the same body and a different body.
Why are amounts integers in the currency's minor unit? Give one concrete thing that would go wrong if they were floats in dollars.
In what order does GET /charges return charges, what does starting_after mean, and how does the caller know there are more?
A declined card and an unsupported currency both fail. How does the API respond to each, and which of them leaves a record behind?

design_prompts.text: Saved responses live in a dict in process memory and are forgotten after 24 hours. What breaks when this service runs on several servers or restarts, and what would you use instead?
list_charges takes a starting_after charge id rather than a page number or an offset. Why might an API used by many merchants choose this, and what does it cost?
create_charge holds store.lock while it asks the card network to approve the payment. What happens to this service under load, and how would you restructure it?

tasks.text: Support ticket #4471 (Acme): "Charge ch_000812 was for $10.00, but the dashboard shows $14.00 refunded. Our agents issued two refunds of $7.00 about 30 minutes apart. How did the second one go through?" Find the cause in the code and explain it.

Support ticket #4502 (Acme): "Our checkout got back ch_000377 with status succeeded, but the customer was never charged, and ch_000377 does not appear when we list our charges. Our client retries POST /charges with the order number as the Idempotency-Key." Find the cause in the code and explain it.
